newsitem.title: USA: US CORPORATE BONDS - New issues take spotlight.
newsitem.headline: US CORPORATE BONDS - New issues take spotlight.

text.p: While corporate bond secondary trading activity remained subdued ahead of Friday's key U.S. employment report the primary sector bustled with activity, players said.
"Most people are pushing to get their financing done ahead of Friday's jobs report," said one high-grade player. "They are trying to beat potentially higher rates."
On Friday, the Labor Department will release the U.S. employment report for May.
Among Wednesday's issuers were three banks that brought a total of $650 million in new supply, syndicate players said.
BBT&T Corp sold $250 million in A3/BBB-plus rated 10-year subordinated notes at 69 basis points over Treasuries. Bear Stearns & Co was lead manager for the deal.

Another $200 million in A2/A-minus rated 10-year notes were sold by Comerica unit, Comerica Bank. The notes were priced to yield a spread of 64 basis points over Treasuries via lead underwriter Salomon Brothers.
Citicorp also issued A2/A rated $250 million in 10-year subordinated notes at 58 basis points over Treasuries via lead underwriter Lehman Brothers.
The new supply was quickly absorbed by the market, dealers said.
"For the most part these deals went very well...the market did better after everything was priced," said one syndicate source.
Still, another $2.75 billion in global debt offerings is expected to hit the market, players said.

On Wednesday, Ford Motor's unit, Ford Motor Credit Corp, launched a $1.0 billion A1/A-plus rated 10-year debt issue via Merrill Lynch & Co. The deal is expected to price at a spread of 60 basis points over Treasuries.
Bayerische Landesbank is also slated to bring a $1.0 billion 10-year global debt offering early next week also via Merrill Lynch, sources said.
Another $750 million 10-year global 144A debt is expected to come from Rheinische Hyppothekenbank, players said.
Turning to the high-yield sector, prices ended the day up 1/8 to 1/4, traders said.
"As a whole, the market was active today with certain sectors trading better than others," said one high-yield trader.
Supermarket sector paper put in a mixed performance, players said.
Grand Union's 12 percent paper was quoted off one point to 76-1/2 bid, 77 offer. Penn Traffic 9-5/8 also fell one point, high-yield traders said.

Quality Food debt gained 3/8 to trade at 100-3/8, and Dominick Finer Foods were seen better bid at 111, players said. In credit specific news, Ralphs Grocery Co debt failed to budge despite an affirmation to the food retailer's debt by Standard & Poor's. S&P also revised the company's outlook to stable from negative.
"I think the action was pretty much already built in to the bonds," said one high-yield trader in response to the rating action.

Turing to new junk issues, Silgan Holdings Inc unit, Silgan Corp issued $300 million in 144A B1/B rated 12-year senior subordinated debentures at 238 basis points over Treasuries. The issue was increased in size by $150 million, market sources said.
